inspection_summary: Inspected all 571 logical lines. The article proves a circle-zero theorem for period polynomials of modular newforms by converting critical L-values into a self-inversive polynomial, reducing its unit-circle restriction to trigonometric sign changes, and supplying coefficient control through Hadamard products, Euler products, classical zero-counting criteria, and a large-weight exponential approximation. Low weights and the finite gap left by analytic thresholds are handled separately, the latter with reported Sage calculations. Fifteen units preserve the distinct mechanisms and their limits. The paper's phrase ‘Riemann hypothesis’ names an analogy for polynomial zeros; it does not establish or test the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function. Formula layout is generally recoverable but contains shifted exponents, radicals, and extraction markers requiring PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Period polynomials encode critical L-values as coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: The period integral and binomial expansion turn the critical values of a modular-form L-function into the coefficients of one polynomial. This is the foundational compression that lets a statement about a list of L-values become a statement about polynomial zero geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the completed L-function normalization, functional equation, period integral, and both coefficient expansions because their normalizations determine all later reciprocal symmetries.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: square-root level factors, powers of i, binomial indices, and factorial normalizations are displaced in extraction. The generating-function mechanism is clear, but exact identities require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The L-function functional equation becomes reciprocal symmetry of polynomial roots
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the functional equation coefficientwise yields a self-inversive relation: every root is paired with its reciprocal transform. This identifies the symmetry circle and motivates the polynomial ‘Riemann hypothesis’ that all roots lie on it.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the interpretation of coefficients as critical values and the comparison with earlier full-level results so the analogy and claimed extension are explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reciprocal transformation and circle radius are readable, but powers, signs, and square-root normalization in the displayed functional equation should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A half-polynomial converts circle zeros into a sign-change count
accepted_units.why_material: The authors package half of the critical values into an auxiliary polynomial, reconstruct the period polynomial by reciprocal reflection, and observe that its unit-circle restriction is a cosine or sine polynomial according to the functional-equation sign. The circle-zero theorem is thereby reduced to producing exactly the required number of real sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the auxiliary definition, reconstruction identity, sign-dependent trigonometric form, main root-location statement, and quantitative-proof roadmap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: coefficient indices, scaling by the level, error exponents, and the phase equation are visually fragmented. Use the semantic reduction confidently, but verify every exact coefficient and root-location formula from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A root-count sign condition becomes an inequality among critical L-values
accepted_units.why_material: For even functional-equation sign, evaluating the auxiliary trigonometric polynomial at a distinguished boundary point forces a nontrivial alternating inequality among critical values. The paper then flags two explanations—unconditional low-weight Hadamard arguments and a conditional argument from the L-function RH—linking polynomial root geometry back to L-value structure.
accepted_units.context_note: This is retained separately because it isolates a necessary sign invariant that later receives two mathematically different proofs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual sign implication is readable; the exact binomial weights, alternating indices, and displayed inequality contain shifted layout and must be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard zero pairing forces monotonicity of completed critical values
accepted_units.why_material: Hadamard factorization pairs real and conjugate zeros, and the known zero strip makes each factor grow to the right of the critical region. This yields monotonicity of the completed L-function at successive critical arguments, with a refined normalized chain for odd functional-equation sign.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes factorization, zero symmetries, the monotonicity statement, and its proof because the later coefficient comparisons repeatedly depend on precisely where monotonicity begins.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Products and absolute-value pairings are partly scrambled, and fractions in the normalized chain are vertically split. Exact factor identities and endpoint inequalities require PDF verification; the factorwise monotonicity argument is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Ramanujan bounds control ratios of L-values in the absolute-convergence range
accepted_units.why_material: The logarithmic derivative of the Euler product, together with bounds on prime-power coefficients, is integrated between two real arguments to dominate a modular-form L-value ratio by an explicit zeta-function ratio. This converts form-dependent coefficients into uniform analytic error bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the logarithmic-derivative expansion, coefficient bound, and integration step so the later level criteria are connected to their uniform input rather than presented as unexplained constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula extraction splits half-integer arguments, powers, and integral limits across lines. The inequality direction and all exponents must be checked from the PDF before numerical reuse.

accepted_units.title: Weight four reduces exactly to one sine or cosine equation
accepted_units.why_material: For the degree-two case, functional-equation sign makes the transformed polynomial either a multiple of z−z⁻¹ or a two-term cosine expression. Monotonicity of adjacent completed L-values gives the exact unit-circle root count, while a ratio estimate locates the roots for large level.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a complete base-case mechanism rather than a numerical example: it handles both signs and explains the asymptotic locations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The core equations are readable, but level powers in convexity estimates and the final error exponent are broken across lines and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Weight six is reduced to two product inequalities at trigonometric extrema
accepted_units.why_material: For weight six, differentiating the unit-circle trigonometric polynomial identifies all relevant extrema. The required four roots are equivalent to prescribed signs at those extrema, which in turn become two multiplicative inequalities among three adjacent completed L-values.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps both functional-equation signs, the critical-point calculation, and the two exact target inequalities so the subsequent Hadamard argument has a clear geometric purpose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient multiplicities and squared terms are formula-dependent, with some arguments and symbols compressed. Verify the exact inequalities and equality conventions from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Factorwise inequalities propagate through the Hadamard product
accepted_units.why_material: An elementary product lemma lifts an additive inequality satisfied by each aligned factor triple to an inequality for products. The proof groups L-function zeros by functional-equation and conjugation symmetries, checks the needed inequality separately for real, critical-line, and off-line groups, and passes to the full Hadamard product.
accepted_units.context_note: The complete grouping case split is retained because it shows the proof does not assume that zeros lie on the critical line.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The zero-group contribution formulas depend on exact absolute values, denominators, and multiplicities. Their strategic role is clear, but each algebraic contribution should be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The L-function RH gives the boundary sign through Taylor-coefficient positivity
accepted_units.why_material: Under the usual RH for the completed modular L-function, the derivatives also have the required zero geometry; symmetry kills odd derivatives and nonnegativity of even central derivatives makes a Taylor comparison prove the boundary inequality. This supplies an illuminating conditional explanation distinct from the unconditional Hadamard proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained as interpretation rather than evidence for RH: the article explicitly presents it as a conditional route explaining the sign pattern.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Derivative superscripts and Taylor coefficients are crowded but semantically recoverable. Exact series coefficients and inequality factors require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Monotone coefficients transfer Pólya–Szegő zero counts to period polynomials
accepted_units.why_material: A classical theorem forces simple, interlacing zeros of sine and cosine polynomials when their coefficients increase. Completed-L monotonicity handles the first comparison, the Euler-product ratio bound makes the remaining comparisons explicit in level and weight, and computation is reserved for the finite set below those thresholds.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the classical criterion, its sign-change basis, translation to L-value coefficient inequalities, explicit sufficient level bound, and the stated failure of this route to remain sharp for large weight.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Interval endpoints, binomial ratios, zeta-ratio powers, and threshold constants are extraction-sensitive. Reported Sage checks are not reproduced here and are not independent certificates.

accepted_units.title: A zero-transparent exponential model controls the large-weight polynomial
accepted_units.why_material: The normalized auxiliary polynomial is decomposed into a dominant truncated-exponential model plus three errors. On the unit circle the dominant model has an explicitly monotone phase and alternating extrema, so a uniform error smaller than its minimum amplitude preserves all required real- and imaginary-part sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the normalization, decomposition, phase analysis, and perturbation criterion together because the root count follows from their interaction, not from coefficient approximation alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence: summation limits, the central term, powers of the level, and the exponential phase are vertically fragmented. The perturbative sign-change mechanism is clear, but exact definitions and bound (6.2) require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Uniform coefficient bounds reduce the large-weight proof to an explicit finite threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The Euler-product ratio estimate bounds the first error, the exponential tail bounds the second, and central-value monotonicity bounds the third. Combining them gives a single explicit inequality in weight and level, a threshold table, and a finite collection of residual forms delegated to computation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes every error source and the threshold transition so analytic coverage and computational remainder are auditable as separate claims.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Constants, factorials, powers, table alignment, and inequality (6.5) are vulnerable to extraction errors and must be checked from the PDF. The statement that Sage confirmed the remainder lacks code, version, precision, and a preserved result table here.

accepted_units.title: Phase perturbation upgrades circle membership to quantitative root locations
accepted_units.why_material: The same exponential approximation yields an explicit leading phase whose regularly spaced zero locations persist under a uniform small error. Evaluating on either side of each predicted phase zero traps one true root, producing the asymptotic location and equidistribution result for both functional-equation signs.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit distinguishes qualitative circle membership from quantitative spacing and records the stability argument connecting them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The phase, error scale, neighborhood width, and transformation back to the original polynomial contain displaced radicals and fractions. Exact localization constants require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Finite residual cases are closed by L-value evaluation and direct sign-change tests
accepted_units.why_material: The authors identify exactly which weights and levels escape the analytic criteria, enumerate newforms in Sage, compute critical L-values at high precision, test the monotone-coefficient inequality when possible, and otherwise verify the needed number of trigonometric sign changes directly. This records the logical role of computation in completing the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained as computational methodology and provenance claim, not as independently reproduced evidence. The worked form illustrates the final sign-change check but does not certify all residual cases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Decimal L-values, interval endpoints, and trigonometric coefficients should be checked against the PDF. More importantly, the source does not preserve Sage version, commands, precision targets, rounding/error certification, exhaustive case list, or machine-readable outputs, so reproducibility and rigor of the finite closure cannot be established from this text alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Functional symmetry becomes a real-variable root-count problem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Encoding critical L-values in a period polynomial transports the L-function functional equation into reciprocal root symmetry; factoring that symmetry through a half-polynomial then turns the desired circle-zero statement into a count of sine or cosine sign changes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This mechanism establishes the paper’s polynomial analogue only; it supplies no implication for the zero locations of the Riemann zeta function or the underlying modular L-function.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: L-function zero geometry constrains polynomial coefficient geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Known confinement and symmetry of L-function zeros yield monotonic critical values through Hadamard factors, while Euler-product bounds make coefficient ratios uniform; those coefficient constraints are precisely what classical trigonometric zero-counting criteria need.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Some low-weight inequalities require more specialized grouped-factor arguments, and the general coefficient criterion fails for specific small cases.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two complementary explanations of the weight-six sign invariant
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same critical-value inequality is proved unconditionally by multiplying inequalities over symmetric zero groups and explained conditionally by positivity of even Taylor coefficients under the L-function RH, separating proof from conceptual interpretation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conditional Taylor route cannot be used as unconditional evidence for the L-function RH; exact factor and derivative identities remain formula-dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Stable zero counts from a dominant phase plus a uniform error budget
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Once a normalized polynomial is uniformly close on the circle to a model with monotone phase and alternating extrema, a strict amplitude-versus-error inequality preserves the full zero count and also traps each root near a predicted phase location.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The preserved count depends on the strict numerical bound; the extracted constants and finite threshold table must be verified before transferring the argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic coverage plus finite computational closure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Two analytic criteria cover complementary weight-level regions and explicitly expose a finite remainder, after which direct high-precision sign-change evaluation is used instead of silently extrapolating the estimates.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper text does not preserve enough computational provenance or error certification to reproduce the finite closure as an exact audit artifact.
